title: BAGELS: Benchmarking the Automated Generation and Extraction of Limitations from Scholarly Text

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the LLM with only the paper's title to summarize the content and checking if it outputs a disclaimer of unfamiliarity, ensuring the evaluation data was not present in the model's training set.
Swapping the input order when comparing texts using an LLM-as-a-judge to ensure consistent results and prevent the model from arbitrarily favoring the first input.
Cross-referencing the LLM's judgments with human evaluations and using multiple different models to prevent a single model from circularly favoring its own generated outputs.
Using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to introduce diverse evidence and source content, reducing the model's tendency to generate generic or overly 'safe' limitation statements.
Grounding all generated limitations in source content and peer reviews via a RAG framework to prioritize factuality over the model's preference for longer or well-written outputs.
